verses.text: At night on my bed, I looked for the one my heart loves. I looked for him, but I did not find him.
I will get up now and go around the city, through the streets and the squares. I will look for the one my heart loves. I looked for him, but I did not find him.
The watchmen who go around the city found me. I asked them, "Have you seen the one my heart loves?"
I had hardly passed them when I found the one my heart loves. I held on to him and would not let him go until I had brought him into my mother's house, into the room of the one who gave birth to me.
Daughters of Jerusalem, I make you promise by the gazelles and by the deer of the field: do not stir up or awaken love until the time is right.
Who is this coming up from the wilderness like columns of smoke, smelling of myrrh and frankincense, and all the spices of the merchants?
Look, it is Solomon's carriage! Sixty strong men surround it, the strongest men of Israel.
They all carry swords and are skilled in war. Each man has his sword at his side, ready for the dangers of the night.
King Solomon made himself a carriage from the wood of Lebanon.
He made its posts of silver, its base of gold, and its seat of purple cloth. Its inside was lovingly decorated by the daughters of Jerusalem.
Come out, you daughters of Zion, and look at King Solomon wearing the crown his mother put on him on his wedding day, the day his heart was filled with joy.
